definition: Thought monitoring is a metacognitive skill involving awareness of and keeping track of one’s own thoughts. In this source, it is described as something that may be improved in therapy alongside emotion regulation.

reasons: The packet does not define thought monitoring as a metacognitive skill or explain it as awareness of and tracking one’s own thoughts; it only mentions therapies aimed at improving thought monitoring.
The therapy-related claim is supportable, but the definition adds an unsupported general definition rather than limiting itself to the source’s wording.

The packet does not define “thought monitoring” as a metacognitive skill involving awareness of and keeping track of one’s own thoughts; it only mentions “thought monitoring” in the context of therapies aimed at improving it.

The definition’s claim that it “may be improved in therapy alongside emotion regulation” is only loosely supported by the single sentence in the packet about therapies aimed at improving both thought monitoring and emotional regulation, but the definition also adds additional substantive content (the specific meaning of the term) that is not supported.

The packet frames “thought monitoring” as part of dysfunctional metacognitive processes related to orthorexia nervosa; the definition generalizes beyond what the packet explicitly states (i.e., it does not limit meaning to that context).
